Interpolation retirement receipt — captured 2026-11-13
=====================================================
MEASURED: expected answers were evaluated ONLY by the existing independent
spike/interpolate_reference.py, under bundled CPython 3.13 (Linux x86_64/libm).
Native output was never used as an expected answer, including refusal records.
The archived generator executes the original seeded input-generation loop
verbatim (random.Random(0x1713)); fixtures freeze those generated inputs too.
No regeneration or archived Python dependency exists in public runtime tests.
Bit parity is qualified for this Python/libm arithmetic contract, not a claim
that every platform's pow implementation produces identical last bits.

All three exact original files are ignored local backups in legacy/retired-rust17.
They are deliberately NOT distributed executable public oracles.

Lossless, dependency-free text format v1
--------------------------------------
One record per line, pipe-separated eleven fields (header in each data file).
Label, route, input rows, width (1 unless skin), requested degree, numeric style,
allowed status, actual output degree, input floats, output controls, full knots.
Style 0/1/2 = Uniform/Chord/SqrtChrd. Float lists use comma-separated 16-digit
IEEE754 binary64 bit-pattern hex (big-endian notation); '-' is an empty list.
No decimal rounding or signed-zero normalization. Input skin data is section
major; output skin data is column major, exactly as the exported ABI specifies.
Refused independent Python cases preserve the ORIGINAL allowed status set
{-2,-4}: the Python exception does not independently assign a C status code.
The fixtures therefore do not pretend to independently distinguish those two.
Invalid-style ABI tests separately require exactly -2.

Integrity and coverage
----------------------
interpolate_math.txt: 7,999,321 bytes, SHA256
10b72d838dae78fc7157c0d55e53276b7cff37519f0de0dd98b23cda3b81e73a
FNV1a64 72d3a1f43fef5688
2025 oracle cases: 759 successful open, 249 periodic, 1005 skin, 12 refusals.
All 80 generated random datasets, every original degree/style and all five
adversarial datasets transfer unchanged (two-point clamp, signed zero,
repeated points, symmetric pivots, pow rounding; degenerate skin column).
Hard signed-zero counts: 978 negative input zeros, 606 negative output zeros,
8499 positive output zeros (controls and knots). Counts are asserted in Rust.
Eight additional original direct-ABI refusals transfer to Rust: three invalid
styles, oversized open/periodic/skin, zero open output capacity, null out-degree.
Total original direct qualification retained: 2013 successes + 20 refusals.
Count-clearing checks are strengthened to initialize all affected counts to 99.

FNV1a64 05e92248199ef716
39 cases: all 36 original numeric size/style adapter cases move into Rust ABI
replay, plus production periodic n=4 and the two original host refusals.
Python retains real production calls at open n=32, skin 8x8, periodic n=4,
requiring exact fixture output AND native counter +1. Actual adapter calls at
open 16/skin 8x8/periodic 6, original thresholds 16/64/3, malformed inputs,
nonfinite/short coordinates, ragged sections, ABI error/malformed count framing
and refusal counter semantics remain host-only. No production threshold edits.
Successful ABI output counts, degree, bit patterns and untouched canary tails
are checked in Rust; Python verifies container reconstruction and host routing.

Performance qualification — preserved, not replaced with a weaker claim
----------------------------------------------------------------------
interpolate_performance_inputs.txt: 163,177 bytes, SHA256
c66898fd51242aa559e82ba215e336fbe9ce395d800dbc56bbd9392ceda01c6c
FNV1a64 7cb39f7561befac0
Nine ORIGINAL independent input datasets, expected controls, knots and degrees.
interpolate_performance_baseline.txt: 994 bytes, SHA256
815bf81f7e8e8476eb1794f4cf6312e333f49513af2504a8d904cd70beef090a
FNV1a64 e8c43e57e3c0bd40
Batch timings are lossless float.hex seconds; repetition counts are unchanged.
Method unchanged: best of five batches for native and independent Python,
then native_seconds / python_seconds <= 0.90 for EACH of the nine workloads.
Open n=16/32/64 (100/40/10 repetitions); skin 8x8/16x16/32x32 (100/30/5);
periodic n=4/16/64 (400/200/50). All captured ratios passed, 0.0814–0.4733.
The preserved original runner also passed 54/54 after capture (all nine ratios
0.084–0.494). Only its root/reference file paths change in the offline copy.

A historical timing cannot robustly assert a 10% relative speedup on arbitrary
hardware, interpreters or load. Therefore the relative criterion is NOT
silently replaced by an absolute deadline or Rust-vs-Rust duplicate algorithm.
The unchanged same-host relative qualification remains a PRIVATE OFFLINE
release/source-qualification step, explicitly deferred from public CI, requiring
the ignored archived reference. Run from repository root:
NARWHAL_PURE_CORE=<absolute qualified release library> PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
 tools/blender-5.2.2-linux-x64/5.2/python/bin/python3.13
 legacy/retired-rust17/qualify_interpolate_offline.py
The exact original source files and capture generator also remain privately
available for audit. Do not claim the public CI alone re-establishes 10% wins.
Main owns integration of this offline qualification into release acceptance.

Public stable protections are independent: exact fixed workload/size hashes,
actual production routing counters, ABI size/capacity bounds and count clearing,
plus replay of all nine qualified workloads ten times with a broad 30-second
runaway-work bound (including debug builds). That bound detects gross stalls;
it is explicitly NOT the original 10% performance qualification. Public CI has
no replaced Python numerical engine or executable arithmetic oracle.

Mutation qualification
----------------------
In an ignored private source copy (production source never edited), the actual
Rust integration tests were RED for each: naive Iterator::sum replacing py_sum;
x*x replacing Python-compatible pow; output signed-zero canonicalization;
uncleared output count on refusal. Exact source restoration made all 3 tests
GREEN. Private logs: legacy/retired-rust17/mutation_results.txt.
Python boundary test was RED against the retired-rust16 core at the original
production open n=32 call, and GREEN against rebuilt release core (31 checks).
Debug and release Rust integration tests both passed (3/3 each).

Scope
-----
No production algorithm, shared manifest, shared gate, geometry or routing
threshold edits. Main owns source qualification/staging, full gate and commit.
The 8MB corpus is transparent fixed DATA, not encoded Python or generated Rust
algorithm code, and is not a language-statistics exclusion or fallback engine.
